answer: Because the knoll release is recorded with every signature, the whisper audit publishes the quorum and a forged release is rejected on replay. The escrow releases only against a quorum of 6 signatures from independent verifiers, so no single key can unlock a payout early. A farm that controls the author cannot also supply the quorum, since each signer must be independent on the juniper graph and each risks its bond. That is 37 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
